suggested_backlog.title: Remediate security and soundness advisories in the locked Rust graph
scope: Cargo.lock: anyhow, event-listener, lru, memmap2, tar, tokio
suggested_backlog.action: Review transitive owners and compatibility before changing versions. OSV fixed boundaries include anyhow 1.0.103, event-listener 5.4.2, memmap2 0.9.11, tar 0.4.46 and tokio 1.53.3. lru has distinct soundness issues with fixed boundaries 0.16.3 and 0.18.2, requiring API/dependency-owner review.
suggested_backlog.gate: Exact locked versions no longer match the listed security/soundness issue groups; supported Linux build/tests pass; independent review records relevant parser, cache, pointer and async-I/O reachability.

suggested_backlog.title: Review and replace unmaintained dependency families
scope: Cargo.lock: bincode, paste, pin-utils, rustybuzz, ttf-parser, zbus_names, zvariant, zvariant_derive
suggested_backlog.action: Review eight deduplicated unmaintained notices (nine locked package versions). Plan supported replacements or time-bounded owner decisions, including compatibility of the D-Bus and rendering dependency families.
suggested_backlog.gate: Each notice has a supported replacement or explicit dated owner decision and replacement plan; changes have relevant serialization/D-Bus/rendering regression evidence. No blanket ignore list.

suggested_backlog.title: Run actual Linux Rust build and tests; retain mock evidence separately
suggested_backlog.action: Run the native daemon build and required real Rust test/format/lint gates in a reviewed Linux toolchain. The existing 10/10 result verifies the audit wrapper with mocks only.
suggested_backlog.gate: Actual cargo build -p bootcontrold and required real test gates have retained exit codes/toolchain/source hashes; the mock suite remains independently green; unavailable gates remain BLOCKED.

suggested_backlog.title: Document historical secret-pattern false-positive triage
suggested_backlog.action: Review the two unit-test entry-token contexts and accessibility-keybinding example. Evidence indicates non-credential contexts; no usable credential was verified and no values are published.

limitations: OSV matches exact locked package versions; it does not establish runtime reachability, active features or application exploitability.
Identifiers and aliases are deduplicated into advisory groups. Unmaintained and unsound notices remain separately labelled; counts of classification labels can overlap.
No application attacks or exploit attempts were run. No external model calls were made. No dependencies were installed and no images were pulled.
Workspace/git/unknown-source packages are unverified, not counted as clean. No real Rust build or Rust tests were run: the cached image has no cargo/rustc.
No values from secret-pattern findings, email addresses, transcripts or host-specific paths are included.
The 10/10 BootControl result exercises audit-wrapper logic using mocked compiler/build/test output. It is not proof that the application compiles or its Rust tests pass.
